To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the retroviral oncogenic v‐myb protein and different C/EPB transcription factors synergize to induce the expression of a gene, mim‐1, which encodes an early response gene in myeloid cell differentiation and that this activation is dependent on C/EBP protein.

(i) the chicken C/EBPB gene encodes a C/EBP protein that is highly expressed and active in myeloid cell lines, (ii) v‐myb activates synergistically with C/EBPB the mim‐1 myeloid gene in fibroblasts, and (iii) c‐myb is active synergistically with CEBPB in fibroblats only at low levels of expression.
the retroviral oncogenes v‐myb (and c‐myb) and C/EBPs are involved in the regulation of the chicken mim gene, which encodes an important transcription factor in the myeloid lineage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of myeloid‐ specific genes by v‐mybs and C/EBPs.
transcriptional regulation by v‐myc, v‐myb, and C/EBPs, and with the role of these transcription factors in myelomonocyte differentiation.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate the expression of the myeloid‐induced mim‐1 gene and with the role of v‐myc in the activation of the gene.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
v‐myb activates the chicken mim‐gene synergistically with C/EBPs.
v‐myb is a potent transcriptional activator of the mim‐ 1 gene, but that its activity is enhanced by C/EBP factors.
the C/EBP proteins are not involved in the activation of mim-1 by v-myb, but rather that they cooperate with v-myb to activate the gene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
v‐myb is not sufficient to activate the mim‐1 promoter and requires C/EBP factors for its activity.

the v‐mybs of the avian and mammalian species are able to activate the mim‐1 promoter synergistically in the presence of the C/EBP proteins, and that the c‐myb of mammals is able to synergize only at low concentrations with the C/EBPs.
the v‐myc and v‐myb oncogenes are not only transcriptional activators, but also transcriptional repressors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the synergistic activation of the mim-1 gene by v-myb and C/ebp transcription factors is a key step in myeloid cell development.
the synergistic activation of the mim-1 gene by v-myb and different CEBP factors is not a peculiarity of the v-myb protein, but a common property of the c-myb and v-myb proteins.
the v‐mybs are not the only factors involved in regulating myeloid‐ specific gene expression.
